Pricing source on every row: **real NSE chain (mid)** = mid of NSE's best bid/ask at the chain's timestamp; **model (BS on NSE chain IV)** = one-sided quote, Black-Scholes on the chain's implied vol; **model (BS on VIX / realised vol)** = no chain today. These are close prices, not fills: an order fills at the next NSE open at the model price (Black-Scholes on the latest chain IV, +1% buy / -1% sell). Write the numeric strikes and the exact expiry date shown here in the order ("ATM" is re-resolved at the fill-day open). **fill est.** = the engine's fill price for the structure if the next open were at today's close (the same chain IV per strike the fill will use, +/-1%): the filled credit or debit will be near it, not near the mids, and it is never re-checked against the strike gap. Only what passes is tabled; each failing structure is one line.

Structures, 1 lot each. Debit: bull call spread (BUY CE ATM, SELL CE ATM+2), bear put spread (BUY PE ATM, SELL PE ATM-2), long straddle (BUY CE + PE ATM): max loss = net debit. Credit: bull put spread (SELL PE below the spot, BUY PE further below), bear call spread (SELL CE above, BUY CE further above), iron condor (both). Credit short strikes = the listed strikes nearest ATM -/+ the expected move (the ATM straddle of that expiry), at least 1 strike step from ATM; each wing 2 strike step(s) beyond its short (1 if not listed or priced); a row that fell back toward ATM says so. A credit structure receives the net credit; max loss = (strike gap - credit) x units + entry charges (condor: the wider side's gap minus the total credit); max gain = credit x units - entry charges. **Margin**: the engine blocks strike gap x units for every short leg (a condor blocks both sides, more than its max loss) and releases it when the short is closed. **PASS/FAIL** is the engine's own check (derivbook.check_open) run on a copy of the book for every leg, in the order the engine fills them (BUY covers first, then SELLs): per-order risk <= 10% of equity (premium for a long leg, margin for a short leg), free cash, free position slots (a condor takes 4), circuit breaker, expiry after the fill day. Each PASS is for that structure alone on today's book: two structures queued together share the slots and the cash, and the engine fills leg by leg, so the second can be left half-built. **Event-trade size: fits** = max loss <= 2% of sleeve equity. **Quotes**: "wide quotes" = a real-chain leg whose ask - bid is over 10% of its mid, or a one-sided quote; "no quote" = the strike has no bid/ask while the ATM does (model price). A labelled row still passes; its credit may exist only on paper. Max loss includes entry charges, not exit charges. **To trade a row**: write ALL its legs in one run, one OPEN per leg in the printed order (covers first), the same decision_date and lots, the numeric strike, the exact expiry and instrument CE / PE exactly (other spellings are not recognised as short options, so such a SELL can be checked before its cover and rejected as naked). To exit, CLOSE every leg by its position id (the engine then closes the short first; without ids a long written first is rejected and dropped).
